economy.summary: Her campaign website, last updated during an earlier election cycle, says she has focused on job growth by promoting the manufacturing and energy industries and has supported job retraining programs for local workers.
economy.short: Promotes job growth through manufacturing, energy industries, worker retraining.

taxes.summary: Voted against the 2025-26 state General Appropriations bill, saying the roughly $50 billion plan spends too much and that covering the revenue gap from the General Fund surplus is unsustainable and would mean future cuts or tax increases.
taxes.short: Voted against 2025-26 budget, saying it spends too much.

abortion.summary: Said the April 2026 Commonwealth Court ruling striking Pennsylvania's ban on Medicaid coverage of abortion was an example of legislating from the bench, and said that despite the ruling she will continue to advocate for the rights of the unborn.
abortion.short: Opposes Medicaid abortion coverage ruling; advocates for the unborn.

education.summary: Criticized House Democrats for repeatedly re-referring three bills (House Bills 158 and 1849, Senate Bill 9) that would limit participation in female sports to biological females, describing the legislation as ensuring safety in women's sports; this is a school-sports measure rather than a broader education platform.
education.short: Backs bills limiting female sports to biological females.

healthcare.summary: Sponsored House Bill 157 to create a Rural Health Care Grant Program that would help pay the education debt of nurses, physicians, midwives and dentists who practice at hospitals and clinics in rural or medically underserved areas, citing a nationwide health care workforce emergency.
healthcare.short: Sponsors grants recruiting health practitioners to rural areas.

energy.summary: Opposes Pennsylvania's participation in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, calling it a multi-state energy tax program that would raise heating and lighting costs and cut energy jobs, and says the legislature rather than the executive branch should set the state's energy policy.
energy.short: Opposes RGGI, calling it an energy tax raising costs.

guns.summary: Voted for Senate Bill 565 in November 2021, which would have removed the requirement to obtain a license to carry a concealed firearm in Pennsylvania; the bill passed both chambers and was vetoed by the governor.
guns.short: Voted to end license requirement for concealed carry.
